name: Lever registry, default deny
objective: Only registered levers can run; an unregistered or unknown lever name is denied and audited, so a fooled model can only press buttons that exist.
implemented_in: core/levers/registry.py; levers/registry.json; core/levers/runner.py

name: Parameter schema validation
objective: Every lever parameter is checked for type, required, enum, length and pattern before anything runs, so malformed or injected values never reach a lever.
implemented_in: core/levers/schema.py

name: Role-based authorization; agents may only dry-run writes
objective: The identity's role must satisfy the lever's required role for the mode; agent identities can propose writes in dry-run but never execute them.
implemented_in: core/identity/store.py; core/levers/runner.py

name: Per-client scope at the tool layer
objective: Every call names one client; the caller must be scoped to it and the lever must be enabled for it (ISO-1), so a technician for one tenant cannot touch another.
implemented_in: core/levers/runner.py; core/identity/store.py

name: Dry-run by default with a diff
objective: Every lever runs in dry-run unless execute is requested; dry-run returns the exact diff and changes nothing, and execute applies exactly that diff.
implemented_in: core/levers/runner.py; core/levers/diff.py

name: Lead approval bound to lever, client and params
objective: Execute on an approval-required lever needs an approval record from a lead scoped to the same client, matching the exact lever, client and canonical params (ISO-9).
implemented_in: core/levers/runner.py (_check_approval); core/levers/models.py (Approval)
evidence: tests/phase1/test_levers.py::test_p1_5_execute_without_lead_approval_denied, ::test_p1_5_execute_with_lead_approval_allowed_and_approver_recorded, ::test_p1_5_invalid_approvals_denied, ::test_p1_5_approver_must_be_scoped_to_the_client; tests/py/backup/test_b68_backup.py::test_b68_2_executing_needs_a_technician_and_a_leads_approval_bound_to_the_job (backup.retry-job); tests/py/levers/test_b28_runner3.py (R3 two-approver policy in the runner); tests/py/queue/test_b28_queue_dual.py, tests/py/ui/test_b28_dual_e2e.py (the queue and page collect a second, different lead; the offline CLIs still run without a policy); tests/py/groups/test_b32_groupops.py::test_b32_1_execute_without_an_approval_is_denied_and_changes_nothing, ::test_b32_1_execute_adds_the_member_with_an_approval_and_an_audit_record; tests/py/mailbox/test_b33_mailboxops.py::test_b33_1_a_failed_dry_run_or_a_refused_execute_leaves_the_file_byte_identical

name: Four-eyes rule (no self-approval)
objective: The requester can never approve their own write; separation of duties between who asks and who allows.
implemented_in: core/levers/runner.py; core/queue/store.py
evidence: tests/phase1/test_levers.py::test_p1_5_invalid_approvals_denied; tests/phase1/test_queue.py::test_only_a_lead_for_the_client_other_than_the_requester_may_decide; docs/DEMO.md step 6 fallback. Limit: approver identity is asserted through the demo identity picker, not authenticated, until C-44 (STD-ID-7)

name: Hash-chained audit log with head pin and verifier
objective: Every lever call, allowed or denied, writes one record (agent, client, lever, redacted params, mode, result, approver, time) chained by SHA-256 with a head pin; a verifier names the first broken record.
implemented_in: core/audit/chain.py; core/audit/verify.py
evidence: tests/phase1/test_audit.py::test_p1_2_one_byte_changed_in_a_middle_record_names_its_seq, ::test_p1_2_deleting_the_last_record_is_caught_by_the_head_pin; tests/phase1/test_levers.py::test_every_call_allowed_or_denied_is_audited_in_one_intact_chain; `uv run python -m core.audit.verify <log>` exit code. Limit: tamper-evident, not tamper-proof (THREAT_MODEL limit 4)

name: Audit before apply
objective: A state change is never saved without its audit record; if saving fails after the record, a second record says so.
implemented_in: core/levers/runner.py (_run)
evidence: code path in core/levers/runner.py (_record before tenant.save); tests/phase1/test_levers.py::test_p1_5_execute_with_lead_approval_allowed_and_approver_recorded

name: Secret redaction before logging
objective: Params named like secrets and values shaped like secrets (bearer tokens, API keys, JWTs, long hex or base64) are redacted before any audit write; DC-6 never lands in a log.
implemented_in: core/audit/redact.py

name: Data minimisation in the audit log
objective: The audit log records identifiers and the diff of changed state, not read results or ticket bodies, so PII/PHI/NPI read by a lever is not copied into evidence (D-017).
implemented_in: partial: core/levers/runner.py (_record writes status, reason, applied, changes; not data); counted partial until a test proves it (STD-DC-1 strict words)
evidence: code review of core/levers/runner.py::_record; docs/DECISIONS.md D-017. No dedicated test asserts read data is absent (gap); planned in B02-3

name: Untrusted input wrapping
objective: Ticket, email, document and tool-output text is normalised and wrapped in a labelled, content-hashed data block before a model sees it; forged delimiters are neutralised.
implemented_in: core/guard/wrap.py; core/guard/normalise.py

name: Prompt-injection tripwire
objective: Transparent rules flag instruction-like text after NFKC and invisible-character stripping; a flagged ticket goes to the security queue with no lever. A tripwire, not the control (D-019).
implemented_in: core/guard/detect.py; evals/injection/corpus.jsonl; evals/injection/report.py; workflows/triage/triage.py
evidence: tests/phase1/test_guard.py::test_p1_7_every_injection_case_is_flagged, ::test_p1_7_no_benign_ticket_is_flagged; tests/phase1/test_triage.py::test_sa2_every_injection_ticket_is_flagged_reported_and_gets_no_lever. 100% only on a 50-case synthetic corpus written with the rules; not a real-world claim

name: Model output cannot choose the lever or its parameters
objective: The model names only a category from a fixed list; a fixed table maps category to at most one lever, and parameters come from ticket form fields, never from ticket text or model output.
implemented_in: workflows/triage/rules.py; workflows/triage/triage.py; core/gateway/gateway.py (text only)

name: Loopback-only model gateway, hosted providers off
objective: Client data never leaves the machine: local models only on 127.0.0.1/localhost/::1, look-alike hosts and redirects refused, hosted adapters disabled stubs.
implemented_in: core/gateway/loopback.py; core/gateway/hosted.py; config/models.json

name: Provider abstraction against lock-in
objective: One gateway interface; model names live only in config; routing per task is a config change, so swapping provider needs no code change (AIR-7).
implemented_in: core/gateway/gateway.py; core/gateway/config.py; config/routing.json; config/models.json

name: Timeouts and failure containment
objective: Each lever runs under its declared timeout against a private state copy; a late, crashing or down component returns an error and applies nothing; providers that are down return an error object.
implemented_in: core/levers/runner.py (_run_with_timeout); core/gateway/gateway.py

name: Idempotency on write levers
objective: A repeated execute of the same lever, client and key fields is a no-op once the desired state is reached, and two concurrent executes cannot interleave; prevents double actions from retries.
implemented_in: partial: core/levers/runner.py (_idempotency key recorded; no-change result; execute lock); no persistent replay-key store or retry tests (Phase 7)

name: Approval queue and viewer hardening
objective: The approval page binds 127.0.0.1 only, checks Host, is POST-only with CSRF, escapes every value, has no script; a proposal is marked approved before execution so a crash cannot run it twice.
implemented_in: ui/app.py; core/queue/store.py
evidence: tests/phase1/test_ui.py::test_sc3_refuses_any_host_but_ipv4_loopback, ::test_csrf_token_is_required, ::test_every_page_has_the_csp_and_no_script, ::test_hostile_values_are_escaped_everywhere; tests/phase1/test_queue.py::test_sc1_reject_changes_nothing_and_is_audited. Gap: approver sign-in is a demo identity picker (see C-44)

name: Read levers cannot write
objective: A lever declared read that changes state has its result discarded and an error recorded, so a mislabelled R0 lever cannot act as a write.
implemented_in: core/levers/runner.py (_run)

name: Output reconciliation (no invented numbers)
objective: Every number in a client-facing summary must reconcile with the computed findings; a mismatch fails the run, so a later model rephrasing cannot invent facts (AIR-3, AIR-4).
implemented_in: levers/powershell/TenantBaseline/Test-SummaryReconciles.ps1
evidence: tests/sliceb/Test-SliceB.ps1 (SB-2 checks); docs/DEMO.md step 5. Today the summary is template-filled, not model-written (D-020); tests/py/advisories/test_b47_advisories.py::test_b47_2_no_number_is_invented_counts_reconcile_to_the_fixtures (fixture-based report counts)

name: Protected paths need owner review
objective: Changes to guard scripts, CI, configuration, governance and the permission and audit code need the owner's review before they merge.
implemented_in: .github/CODEOWNERS; docs/BRANCHING_RELEASE.md
evidence: docs/THREAT_MODEL.md section 3. CODEOWNERS is advisory until branch protection is enabled in the repository settings

name: Commit-time secret scan
objective: Commits containing secret-shaped content or secret filenames are refused before they enter history.
implemented_in: scripts/hooks/pre-commit; scripts/install-hooks.ps1
evidence: scripts/hooks/pre-commit. Heuristic; off until install-hooks runs

name: CI with least-privilege token and pinned actions
objective: Every PR runs the lint, type and test suites on clean runners with a read-only token and version-pinned actions before merge.
implemented_in: .github/workflows/ci.yml
evidence: tests/py/tools/test_b07_ci_wiring.py::test_b07_1_every_action_is_pinned_to_a_full_commit_sha, ::test_b07_1_the_token_stays_read_only, ::test_b07_1_ci_runs_the_roadmap_item_tests_and_the_demo_smoke_test (static checks of the committed file); permissions: contents: read in ci.yml. Run history lives on GitHub (D-021) and is not re-checked offline

name: Data classification and pre-prompt redaction gate
objective: Every input carries a data class (DC-0 to DC-6); each tenant has an industry floor (dental = DC-4, financial = DC-5); PHI, NPI and secrets are removed or tokenised before any model call, and unknown text is treated as the floor.
implemented_in: core/guard/classify.py; core/guard/redact_prompt.py; core/gateway/gateway.py (B-55: every gateway call carries a data class, the floor comes from the client record, shapes are tokenised before any provider, DC-6 blocks the call)

name: Per-tenant retrieval isolation
objective: RAG retrieval filters by client in the store or query layer (one index or namespace per tenant), never by prompt instruction; refusal when no source; citations required (ISO-2).
implemented_in: partial: core/levers/handlers.py (kb.search reads only the client's own articles); rag/ planned for Phase 5
evidence: tests/phase1/test_levers.py::test_p1_1_kb_search_only_sees_the_clients_own_articles; planned Phase 5 leakage eval (client A must never see client B)

name: Tenant isolation of prompts, context, logs and error text
objective: One model call carries one client's data; no memory, cache or few-shot examples are shared across tenants; prompt logs and exports are per tenant; errors never echo another tenant's data (ISO-3 to ISO-7).
implemented_in: partial: workflows/triage/triage.py (one prompt per ticket); audit records carry a client field (core/audit/chain.py); no enforcement assertion or per-client export yet; per-client adapters and reports: adapters/backup, adapters/alerts, workflows/backup_review, workflows/alerts, workflows/advisories, workflows/expiry
evidence: partly built, tests: tests/py/backup/test_b68_backup.py::test_b68_3_a_job_of_another_client_is_never_listed_counted_drafted_or_printed; tests/py/alerts/test_b43_alerts.py::test_b43_1_a_group_never_mixes_clients; tests/py/lockout/test_b39_lockout.py::test_b39_1_another_clients_user_answers_like_an_absent_one; tests/py/advisories/test_b47_advisories.py::test_b47_1_a_file_for_another_client_is_refused_and_never_joined. Still planned: planned: test that a multi-ticket batch never mixes clients in one gateway call; per-client audit export filter test

name: Hosted AI provider approval gate
objective: A hosted provider can be enabled only with a recorded approval, written retention and training terms, a BAA covering the exact service and configuration where DC-4 may be present, and a per-tenant data-handling setting that allows it.
implemented_in: core/gateway/hosted.py; core/gateway/vendor_register.py; governance/ai-vendor-register.json (B-90: a hosted call needs an approved, in-date register entry naming the client, purpose and data class; the shipped register is all pending, so nothing hosted runs)

name: Risk class and version on every lever, enforced by class
objective: Each registry entry declares risk_class (R0-R3), owner and semantic version; the runner enforces the HO rules for the class (approvals, verification, caps); the audit record names the version that ran.
implemented_in: partial: core/levers/models.py requires risk_class on every write lever and carries an integer lever_version; core/levers/runner.py enforces the class (approver minimum, two leads for R3, risk-class default caps) and writes lever_version into every audit record. An owner field and semantic versions are planned

name: Requester identity verification for access-affecting levers
objective: Before an R2 identity lever (MFA reset, disable, session revoke) executes, the affected person or their manager is verified out of band (callback to the number on file) and the verification is recorded with the approval.
implemented_in: core/levers/runner.py; core/levers/oob.py (B-02, B-28: an execute of a lever that requires requester verification is denied without a recorded verification {method, by, at}; R3 identity levers need a callback to the number on file plus a contact confirmation)

name: Kill switch per lever and per tenant
objective: Any lead or on-call engineer can pause a lever globally or for one tenant immediately, without approval; paused levers deny with a clear reason and the pause is audited.
implemented_in: core/levers/pause.py; core/levers/runner.py (B-02: a lead pauses a lever for every client or for one client without approval; paused levers deny dry-run and execute with the reason; pause and resume are audited)
evidence: tests/py/levers/test_b02_runner_gates.py::test_b02_1_global_pause_denies_dry_run_and_execute_with_the_reason, ::test_b02_1_client_pause_stops_only_that_client, ::test_b02_1_pause_and_resume_each_write_one_audit_record, ::test_b02_1_pausing_needs_no_approval_and_no_second_person. Only a lead may pause; an on-call role is not modelled

name: Blast-radius and rate limits
objective: Each write lever has caps: targets per run, executes per tenant per hour, tenants per change; R2 is one target per approval; bulk or cross-tenant runs need R3 approval.
implemented_in: partial: core/levers/caps.py (B-42: targets per run, executes per client per hour and clients per day from the registry, with a risk-class default so no write lever is uncapped; counted from the audit chains). One target per R2 approval and R3 approval for bulk or cross-tenant runs are planned (the R2 default is 10 targets per run)

name: Rollback from recorded before-state
objective: Every applied write records the changed fields before and after, so the affected person can be restored first; each R1/R2 lever gets a tested undo lever.
implemented_in: partial: core/levers/diff.py and core/levers/runner.py (audit result.changes holds the diff); undo levers planned
evidence: audit records from tests/phase1/test_levers.py::test_p1_3_execute_applies_exactly_the_dry_run_diff carry changes; planned: undo-lever round-trip tests (apply, undo, state byte-identical)

name: Wrong-automated-action incident runbook
objective: A written, rehearsed procedure: detect, contain (kill switch), restore the person, scope from the audit chain, assess HIPAA/GLBA impact, notify, fix through change management, blameless review (IR-1 to IR-9).
implemented_in: docs/runbooks/ai-incident-response.md (IR-1 to IR-9 with commands); docs/TABLETOP_2026.md (a scripted tabletop on a synthetic wrong disable at Contoso Dental) (B-94)
evidence: tests/py/governance/test_b94_incident_response.py::test_b94_1_runbook_commands_run_end_to_end_on_a_synthetic_wrong_disable, ::test_b94_3_every_ir_step_is_recorded_with_a_time_in_order (synthetic tenants; no real incident and no people-time exercise)

name: Notification templates and timelines
objective: Plain-language templates for the affected person, the client contact and the client's privacy or security officer, with internal deadlines that leave the client time for HIPAA (60-day outer limit for BA to CE), FTC Safeguards (30 days, 500+ consumers) and state law.
implemented_in: partial: governance/templates/notifications/ (plain-language drafts for the affected person, the client contact and the privacy officer, each sent by a person) and workflows/notify/ (per-lever notices). The internal deadlines are listed as confirm-with-counsel; nobody has reviewed them

name: End-user fast path back
objective: One phone number and reply address reach a human; automation-affected tickets are auto-prioritised; restore-access target agreed with the MSP; a person can always ask for a human instead of an automated reply (EU-2, EU-7).
implemented_in: partial: workflows/notify/ (B-04: every notice to an affected person says what changed, why, who to contact and how to get it back). A PSA priority rule for automation-affected tickets and a restore-time metric are planned
evidence: tests/py/notify/test_b04_notify.py::test_b04_3_t3101_draft_says_what_why_who_back_and_undo; planned: PSA priority rule and monthly restore-time metric

name: Lever change management with staged rollout
objective: Lever changes arrive as reviewed PRs with green CI, then roll out test tenant, pilot client tenant, 10%, all; the previous version stays pinnable per tenant; emergency changes are re-reviewed (CM-1 to CM-7).
implemented_in: partial: .github/workflows/ci.yml and PR-only merges after the owner's yes (D-021); the lever_version audit field is written by core/levers/runner.py. Rollout rings and per-tenant version pinning are planned
evidence: tests/py/tools/test_b07_ci_wiring.py::test_b07_1_ci_runs_the_roadmap_item_tests_and_the_demo_smoke_test; tests/py/levers/test_b28_runner3.py::test_b28_4_every_record_carries_request_id_actor_kind_and_lever_version; PR history and CI runs on the private repo; planned: ring assignment file

name: Agent and technician access review; least-privilege delegated access
objective: Quarterly review of every agent and human identity, its role and client list; MSP access to each tenant uses per-tenant least-privilege delegated roles (GDAP), no standing Global Admin, and lever scope never exceeds delegated access (ISO-10).
implemented_in: partial: workflows/access_review/ (B-49: a dated, hashed quarterly export of every agent and technician identity, its role and client list, decided row by row by a lead) and the GDAP Global Administrator listing in workflows/expiry/ (B-54); identities are a static synthetic file (config/identities.json). A check that lever scope never exceeds delegated access is planned

name: Write-once audit head pinning and retention
objective: The audit head hash is pinned in storage the writer cannot rewrite (immutable blob or external log), records are retained at least six years where HIPAA documentation applies, and per-client exports are available.
implemented_in: partial: core/audit/verify.py checks a chain against a head pinned outside it, and core/audit/sqlite_store.py refuses update and delete (B-17, B-82). Write-once storage (an immutable blob) and a retention policy are planned; the Bicep in infra/ has not been compiled

name: Monitoring and alerting on automation behaviour
objective: Alerts on denial spikes, after-hours executes, approvals faster than a human could read the diff, cross-client denials, verifier failures and injection flags per tenant.
implemented_in: partial: workflows/monitoring/ (B-83: versioned alert rules replayed over audit and gateway records: audit-chain failure, breaker open, budget exhaustion, approval backlog age, dead-letter growth). Alerts on denial spikes, after-hours executes, approvals faster than a diff can be read, cross-client denials and injection flags are planned

name: Evaluation gate before promotion
objective: A workflow, prompt, model or routing change is promoted only if its golden-set eval meets the recorded threshold, the injection corpus still passes, and corrections from the pilot tenant are reviewed; R1 autonomy needs 30 days of shadow mode.
implemented_in: partial: evals/triage/report.py, evals/injection/report.py, workflows/triage/corrections.py; no threshold gate in CI yet

name: Staff training and acceptable use
objective: Technicians and account managers know what may enter a prompt, how to read a proposal and diff, what an approval means, and how to report an AI incident.
implemented_in: partial: governance/STAFF_TRAINING.md, governance/CLIENT_CONVERSATION_GUIDE.md and governance/ACCEPTABLE_USE.md (document-only), checked by workflows/training/ (B-92, B-96). No one has taken the training and there are no completion records

objective: Each AI provider, model host and MCP server is listed with data classes allowed, retention and training terms, BAA or DPA status, ZDR or modified abuse monitoring status, region, and review date.

objective: The prototype never holds real client or ticket data; every metric is labelled fixture-based; anything unverified is labelled unverified.
